hints.title: Keep the same index
hints.body: The hypothesis compares an with bn+cn at the same n. The minimum of b and the minimum of c might occur in different rows.
hints.recap: Separate minima may not occur together.
hints.pitfall: Replacing both entries by their separate minima can create a pair that never appears.
hints.pause: Construct two integer row types in which the minimum of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow></math> and the minimum of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow></math> occur in different rows. Compare their row sums with the sum of the separate minima.

recall.reminder: Extrema of expressions sharing an input must be checked at the same input.

hints.title: Test the minima with legal rows
hints.body: Repeat your two different row types to make 100 rows. Try choosing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow></math> equal to each row sum, then examine a separate example where all <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>a</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow></math> are strictly smaller than their row sums.
hints.recap: The hypothesis is an upper bound and allows strict inequality.
hints.pitfall: Each example must satisfy the premise in every row.
hints.pause: Calculate the minima in your examples and test both proposed minimum bounds.

recall.reminder: The hypothesis is an upper bound and allows strict inequality.

hints.title: Find a bound valid in every row
hints.body: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow></math> be the separate maxima of the two sequences. Compare an arbitrary <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow></math> with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow></math>, then combine that comparison with the hypothesis.
hints.recap: The maximum of a finite list obeys any upper bound valid for every entry.
hints.pitfall: The separate maxima need not occur in the same row to provide an upper bound.
hints.pause: Write the full inequality chain and decide what it establishes about statement III.

recall.reminder: The maximum of a finite list obeys any upper bound valid for every entry.

solution:
I is false. Use 50 rows with (a, b, c)=(1, 0, 1) and 50 with (1, 1, 0). Every row satisfies a≤b+c, but mina=1 while minb+minc=0.

II is false. Set an=0, bn=cn=1 in every row. The hypothesis holds, but mina=0<2=minb+minc.

III is true. If B=maxb and C=maxc, then for each n, an≤bn+cn≤B+C. Therefore maxa≤B+C.

Answer D: III only.
knowledgePattern: Independent minima cannot be combined; maxima give a uniform bound
